edges.description: The model reproduces the multisystem picture, with reduced survival, neuromuscular dysfunction, reduced growth, hepatomegaly and ocular abnormalities including an abnormal retinal ganglion cell layer. The last of these is notable given that biallelic NDUFS2 variants have also been reported in an optic neuropathy.
edges.limitations: Several of the morphological findings, such as an uninflated swim bladder and yolk retention, have no human counterpart and are markers of general larval ill health rather than disease-specific phenotypes. edges.description: One functional allele produces no overt phenotype and no significant decrease in complex I function, despite a significant reduction in Ndufs2 messenger RNA. The model therefore does not reproduce the disease, and that negative result is the point: it is direct evidence that the human condition requires biallelic loss and that heterozygous carriers should be unaffected.
edges.limitations: A hemizygous deletion is not the human genotype, which is biallelic missense. The model shows that halving message is tolerated; it says nothing about what a missense allele in the quinone-binding site does, and it was designed to address ageing rather than this disease. Mouse and human dosage sensitivity for complex I subunits also need not match.

edges.description: Complete loss of Ndufs2 in the brain produces perinatal mortality, reproducing the severity of the human neonatal presentation, and the NDI1 rescue localises the lethal defect specifically to loss of mitochondrial NADH oxidation rather than to some other function of the subunit.
edges.limitations: A brain-restricted complete knockout is neither the tissue distribution nor the allele type of human disease, in which every tissue carries biallelic missense variants with residual function. The model therefore speaks to the consequence of losing NADH oxidation in the brain, not to the multisystem course or to genotype-phenotype relationships.

nodes.description: A conditional knockout restricting Ndufs2 loss to the brain, which is what makes it viable to birth at all, since global deletion is embryonic lethal. nodes.description:
The second, structural arm. Complex I has 45 subunits, seven encoded in mitochondrial DNA and 38 imported, and many of the disease variants reported across its peripheral core subunits fall at subunit interfaces. Modelling seventeen human variant positions as thirty-one mutants in the homologous Escherichia coli enzyme produced a range of reduced activity, and assembly assays, time-delayed expression and co-immunoprecipitation showed that assembly was disrupted.
The per-allele results are what make this node useful rather than generic, and they split the NDUFS2 alleles in two. Modelled R228Q showed a severe assembly defect: NuoCD and NuoI were no longer co-immunoprecipitated with NuoG. Modelled R138Q and Y141C did the opposite, retaining greatly diminished activity even when assembled normally. So the same subunit produces assembly lesions and catalytic lesions depending on which residue is hit, and the two arms of this entry are allele-dependent rather than competing accounts of one lesion.
What keeps this PROVISIONAL is the system rather than the specificity. The work was done in a homologous bacterial enzyme, with human residues mapped onto their E. coli equivalents, so the assembly pathway is analogous rather than identical and the human consequence is inferred.

nodes.description:
Liver disease is part of the fatal neonatal presentation and has a characterised morphology: hepatocyte hypereosinophilia with microvesicular steatosis, and mitochondrial hyperplasia on ultrastructural examination. The reporting authors make a practical point about it, which is that the morphology supported the diagnosis before the genetic testing returned. Hepatomegaly is also present in the ndufs2 knockout zebrafish and is one of the two phenotypes rescued by folic acid there.
PROVISIONAL because the human evidence is a single autopsy case, and the frequency of hepatic involvement across NDUFS2 patients is not established.

nodes.description:
The cellular endpoint, and it is not only an energy deficit. A CRISPR knockout of NDUFS2 in human embryonic kidney cells reduces growth, complex I-specific respiration, glycolytic capacity, ATP pool and membrane integrity, while increasing reactive oxygen species production, apoptosis and necrosis. Complex II respiration rises, which is the expected compensatory shift when the complex I entry point to the chain is blocked and complex II is intact.
In an ndufs2 knockout zebrafish, complex I enzyme activity falls by 80 percent and unbiased metabolomics shows raised lactate, raised tricarboxylic acid cycle intermediates and raised acylcarnitines, so the block propagates into fatty acid oxidation and the cycle as well as into oxidative phosphorylation.

nodes.description:
The catalytic arm of the lesion, and the more precisely characterised of the two. N2 is the last iron-sulfur cluster in the electron relay and the one that reduces ubiquinone. It sits at the NDUFS2-NDUFS7 interface, ligated by four cysteines in NDUFS7 and positioned about 12 angstroms above the quinone-binding site, with NDUFS2 residues forming its second coordination sphere. NDUFS2 therefore controls the cluster without holding it, which is what makes an NDUFS2 defect able to remove it. A conserved arginine near the cluster, which is post-translationally dimethylated, turns out to be required for the cluster to form or to remain stable: substituting it abolishes quinone-reductase activity, the N2 signature disappears from the electron paramagnetic resonance spectrum, and cryo-electron microscopy shows the cubane cluster simply absent from an otherwise intact enzyme. The same substitution also disorders nearby elements of the quinone-binding site.
That last point is what makes this node worth separating from the assembly node, but the claim it licenses is narrower than it first appears. What the structure shows is that a particle which does assemble can be structurally native-like and catalytically dead. It does not show that the amount of enzyme is normal: in the same experiments, complex I content fell to about 40 percent and 25 percent of wild type for the two substitutions, and the authors state plainly that mutations of this residue impair assembly and stability as well. R121 is therefore a residue that hits both arms of this entry at once, which is consistent with the allele-dependent picture rather than an exception to it.

nodes.description:
NDUFS2 encodes the 49 kDa subunit, one of the fourteen core subunits required for catalysis rather than one of the accessory subunits. It is a peripheral-arm subunit sitting at the interface between the membrane and matrix arms of the enzyme, the region that binds ubiquinone and that is also where complex I inhibitors bind.
The reported disease alleles are missense changes at conserved residues. The original report found three, in three families, identified by sequencing NDUFS2 complementary DNA in enzymatically complex I-deficient patients. Later reports include compound heterozygous and homozygous alleles, and at least one patient carried heterozygous changes in both NDUFA8 and NDUFS2, which the reporting authors flagged as raising the possibility of unconventional inheritance in complex I defects rather than as an established digenic mechanism.

nodes.description: A heterozygous mouse, made to ask whether the modest decline in complex I subunit expression seen in ageing is itself harmful. For this disease it is informative in a different way: it is the carrier state, and it shows what a single functional NDUFS2 allele is sufficient for.

The commonest destination. Complex I deficiency is the commonest biochemical cause of the Leigh syndrome spectrum, and NDUFS2 appears among the nuclear Leigh genes detected by sequencing in national cohorts. Progressive leukoencephalopathy is a separate presentation within the same clinical range, and unspecified encephalomyopathy a third.
